title: Microsoft Agent 365: registry sync from external AI platforms
summary: The briefing passes: its licensing, connection controls and synchronization limitations are supported by the current Microsoft documentation. Two minor corrections remain: complete the checklist's connection-creation path and remove synchronization checklist steps that have no corresponding controls-table row.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The Agent 365 AI administrator creates and manages connections in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The platform administrator owns the source account and prepares its credentials and permissions.
claims.quote: The platform administrator controls the source account and its credentials; the Agent 365 administrator manages the connection and reviews the resulting inventory.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Registry sync is admin-opt-in: synchronization requires an administrator-created connection and an initial synchronization.
claims.quote: Connect: Create and validate the connection in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Synchronize: Start synchronization so that Agent 365 discovers supported agents and adds them to the agent registry.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions, Change & support
claims.claim: Synchronization runs are manual and initiated by an administrator.
claims.quote: After you save the connection, select Sync agents to start synchronization. You need to manually synchronize the agents.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Synchronization does not currently run on a schedule.
claims.quote: Manual synchronization only. Agent 365 doesn't currently sync on a schedule, and Microsoft doesn't prescribe a fixed synchronization interval.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Deleting an agent on the source platform does not guarantee its removal from the Microsoft 365 registry.
claims.quote: Synchronization doesn't currently guarantee that an agent removed from the source platform is automatically removed from the Microsoft 365 agent registry.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The general connection guide instructs administrators to select Sync agents after saving the connection.
claims.quote: After you save the connection, select Sync agents to start synchronization.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The Databricks Genie guide says saving the connection starts its first synchronization automatically.
claims.quote: When you save the connection, the details pane opens and starts the first synchronization.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout, After rollout
claims.claim: Subsequent Databricks Genie synchronizations use Sync agents.
claims.quote: To synchronize after you create or share more Genie agents, open the connection and select Sync agents.

claims.claim: Registry sync provides visibility and governance but does not add code-level Agent 365 capabilities.
claims.quote: Registry sync doesn't add code-level capabilities. It provides visibility and governance for agents you don't build or host yourself.

claims.claim: Registry sync does not require code changes to the agents.
claims.quote: Registry sync (the connected platforms feature described in this article) gives you visibility and governance for agents that you don't build or host yourself. It doesn't require code changes.

claims.claim: Learn documents an available connection workflow despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: Use the Connected platforms page to connect supported third-party agent platforms to Microsoft Agent 365. After you create a connection, Agent 365 can discover supported agents and add them to the Microsoft 365 agent registry.

claims.claim: The integration-options page labels registry sync as preview.
claims.quote: | Registry sync (preview) | Connected agent platforms, such as Google Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock. | Configured per platform. Imports agents for visibility and governance. | No |

claims.claim: Synced external agents appear in the same inventory as other organizational agents.
claims.quote: Agent 365 can synchronize supported agents from connected platforms into the Microsoft 365 agent registry, where they appear with other agents in the organization's inventory.

claims.claim: Registry coverage depends on the source platform and does not guarantee inclusion of every agent there.
claims.quote: Coverage depends on the connected platform and the agents it exposes, so a registry entry represents the supported information available from that source - not a guarantee that every agent on the platform is included.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Agent 365 stores connection credentials as encrypted connection data within Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Agent 365 stores the credentials that you enter for a connection as encrypted connection data within Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Every currently supported platform needs a key-based credential such as an API key, secret or private key.
claims.quote: Every currently supported platform requires a key-based credential, such as an API key, secret, or private key.

claims.claim: Connected platforms does not currently support workload identity federation or role assumption.
claims.quote: Keyless authentication options, such as workload identity federation or role assumption, aren't currently supported for Connected platforms.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Collect agent observability data is enabled by default for new connections.
claims.quote: New connections have this setting enabled by default.

claims.claim: Observability collection retrieves source-platform agent activity telemetry using the stored connection credentials.
claims.quote: When you enable this setting, Microsoft 365 retrieves agent activity telemetry—such as agent sessions, usage, and related operational signals—from the connected platform by using the connection's stored credentials.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Telemetry retrieval may query provider services such as Google BigQuery or Amazon S3 and incur provider-billed access or query charges.
claims.quote: Retrieving agent telemetry from the connected platform might query the provider's own logging or data services (for example, Google BigQuery or Amazon S3) and can incur data access or query charges that the provider bills.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity, Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Connections are read-only by design and Agent 365 never invokes or interacts with the source agents.
claims.quote: Connected platform connections are read-only by design: Agent 365 never invokes, executes, or interacts with agents in the source platform.

claims.claim: Agent 365 does not write to the source platform except when an administrator explicitly removes a synchronized agent.
claims.quote: Agent 365 doesn't write to, modify, or delete resources in the source platform. The only exception is an explicit administrator action to remove a synchronized agent

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Source-agent removal requires a separate optional delete permission that administrators can choose not to grant.
claims.quote: The only exception is an explicit administrator action to remove a synchronized agent, which requires a separate, optional delete permission that you can choose not to grant.

claims.claim: The Google Vertex AI guide lists aiplatform.reasoningEngines.delete among service-account permissions to grant.
claims.quote: Grant the service account the Vertex AI permissions required for agent discovery and management: aiplatform.reasoningEngines.list aiplatform.reasoningEngines.get aiplatform.reasoningEngines.delete

claims.claim: Databricks Genie activity collection requires Can Manage permission.
claims.quote: Activity requires Can Manage. Databricks returns the conversations of all users of a Genie agent only to principals that have Can Manage permission.

claims.claim: With Can Manage permission, removing a synced Genie agent in Agent 365 moves it to the trash in Databricks.
claims.quote: The only exception is when an administrator removes a synchronized agent in Agent 365 and the service principal has Can Manage permission on the Genie agent. In that case, Agent 365 moves the Genie agent to the trash in Databricks.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Agent 365 calls source APIs from fixed outbound IP addresses that restricted source networks must allow.
claims.quote: Agent 365 calls source platform APIs from a fixed set of outbound IP addresses. If your organization restricts network access to a source platform, allow traffic from these addresses before you create the connection.

claims.claim: Source-network restrictions can produce an authentication error even with correct credentials.
claims.quote: When a network restriction blocks Agent 365, the connection can fail with the message Authentication failed. Please check your credentials and try again., even when the credentials are correct.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose; Open questions

claims.claim: Clearing Collect agent observability data stops new collection for that connection's agents.
claims.quote: When you clear this setting, Microsoft 365 stops collecting new observability data for that connection's agents.

claims.claim: Previously collected telemetry remains subject to existing retention and management behavior after collection is disabled.
claims.quote: The agent registry retains telemetry collected earlier according to its existing retention and management behavior.

claims.claim: The registry-sync documentation describes no end-user experience change.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified rollout mechanics for external-platform registry sync.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, Create the connection

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to start and re-run Sync agents, but the controls table contains no corresponding synchronization row.
claims.quote: Start synchronisation ... Re-run Sync agents on a cadence you choose ... Controls: Creating, editing and deleting connections; Whether observability data is collected; Tenant-wide switch to turn registry sync off.
claims.fix: Remove the 'Start synchronisation' and 'Re-run Sync agents' checklist bullets because synchronization has no controls-table row. Retain the verified synchronization explanation in What's changing; do not add a row during correction.

claims.claim: The platform administrator creates source credentials and grants the source-platform permissions.
claims.quote: The platform administrator creates the source-platform credentials, grants the required permissions, and enables platform-side telemetry when applicable.

claims.claim: Credential rotation, source-scope changes and revoking access follow the relevant provider guide.
claims.quote: When you need to rotate credentials, change the source scope, revoke access, or remove the connection, follow the relevant provider guide.
